- When sentiment is positive (≥0.27) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the forecast peak to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.23) and forecast is flat or slightly rising, adjust downward to reflect bearish momentum.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), model should not overcorrect upward; cap forecast gains.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially in 30d horizon) are common — apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid premature peak.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.18) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions; avoid abrupt swings in 30d horizon.  
- In low-sentiment periods, forecast should align with recent 10–15 day mean, not extrapolate from 30d trend.  
- When sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model should not overreact — forecast should lag slightly to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
